runs.text: This is a perfect quality of life. Israel is here. Ninety-two out of a hundred, on the UN's Human Development Index. Health, education, income. What's in the gap? Poverty: one in five Israelis. Prices: fourth highest of thirty-eight rich countries. And Israel is only twenty-seventh. Iceland is first. Now zoom out. They picture Israel as a poor, backward place. Poor and backward looks like this: around sixty-six, the UN's average for medium development. The Emirates, ninety-four. Saudi Arabia, ninety. Turkey, eighty-five. Iran, eighty. Jordan and Egypt, seventy-five. Lebanon, seventy-five. Only one neighbour is closer to utopia. One honest catch: the Emirates beat us. Fifteenth in the world. We're not perfect. We know it. But poor and backward? Not even close.
